decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: sanityCheck receives vector<int4>* loadcounts and passes the same object to JumpModel::sanityCheck; addresstable, loadpoints and partialTable are member state whose mutations survive either exception. recoverAddresses supplies member loadpoints plus a fresh cumulative loadcounts only when collectloads is true. Both fixture sides output pointer-presence observations, loadcounts, member tables, partial state, typed kind/mode/message and warnings at the catch boundary.
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: sanityCheck order is override return -> save original size -> at most two isReachable predecessor iterations -> single-target thunk discriminator -> model sanity -> successful truncation warning. isReachable updates parent only after a recognized constant CBRANCH whose surviving edge reaches the current parent; sizeOut!=2, non-CBRANCH and nonconstant conditions continue without updating parent. recoverAddresses order is recoverModel -> table-size check -> buildAddresses -> sanityCheck -> collapse only on collectloads success. Events expose recover>build>sanity>collapse and every early stop.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: The original table size is captured only after the override return and is compared only after successful model sanity. The single-target absolute offset difference is compared strictly greater than 0xffff. Fixture recover/build/sanity counters start at zero; build records whether loadpoints/loadcounts pointers are present. Fresh JumpBasic production LOAD records are appended with num=1 and cumulative loadcounts are recorded after each emulated switch value; num>1 arises only after collapse or decode/clone, not at the fresh collapse producer boundary.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: LoadTable::operator< compares the full Address only: address-space index before offset, with no size/num tie-break. Address addition wraps through the entry's AddrSpace for both initial contiguous scan and post-sort nextaddr. The pinned GCC 16.2.1 libstdc++ std::sort uses threshold 16, introsort, heap fallback and final insertion sort; its 17-element equal-address permutation is observable because collapse subsequently compares size. Rust reproduces that pinned implementation, while cross-toolchain equivalent-key order remains an explicit MISMATCH residual.

oracle_toolchain.std_sort_contract: Observable reproduction of this pinned libstdc++ implementation only; the C++ standard does not specify equivalent-key order.

residuals.detail: This write-set excludes flow/funcdata, so production must still consume recover_addresses_classified/try_recover_classified and preserve FailThunk separately from FailNormal.

branches.detail: Legacy bool/Option adapters collapse both JumpTableRecoveryError variants, unlike locked stageJumpTable's distinct catch clauses.

residuals.detail: LoadTable::operator< intentionally has no tie-break and the C++ standard leaves equivalent-key std::sort order unspecified. Rust currently reproduces the pinned GCC16 implementation for this oracle, not every supported STL/toolchain.

branches.detail: A different standard-library sort may change the later size-sensitive collapse result; portability requires pinning the production C++ oracle toolchain or defining and validating an implementation-independent contract.
